content:
Hi all,

We would like to announce StatsMLlib, a Lean 4 library for probability, statistics, and learning theory, built upon Mathlib.

  • Repository: https://github.com/Lean-MoDS/StatsMLlib
  • Website (overview, book map, selected theorems): https://statsmllib.github.io/
  • Organizer: @Fanghui Liu, Jason D. Lee, Peter Bartlett, Weijie Su, Taiji Suzuki, Yuekai Sun, Aleksandar Mijatović, @Sho Sonoda
  • Contributors: Yuanhe Zhang, @Sho Sonoda, @Kei TSUKAMOTO, Kazumi Kasaura, @Naoto_ONDA, @Yuma Mizuno, @Kevin Han Huang, and [your name!]

It currently consists of 89 modules (~65k lines) on Lean and Mathlib v4.32.0. The public source contains no sorry, axiom, admit or native_decide. It unifies material that was previously developed in two separate repos (lean-stat-learning-theory and lean-rademacher).

A sample of what is in there:

  • Metric entropy and chaining: covering and packing numbers, Dudley's entropy integral and a truncated variant for sub-Gaussian processes (dudley, truncated_dudley_entropy_bound)
  • Concentration: Efron–Stein, Hoeffding, McDiarmid, Gaussian Poincaré, Gaussian log-Sobolev, Gaussian Lipschitz concentration, Hanson–Wright, matrix Bernstein
  • Linear algebra: SVD, Courant–Fischer, Eckart–Young–Mirsky, Weyl, Davis–Kahan
  • Learning theory: symmetrization, Massart's lemma, Rademacher complexity, uniform deviation bounds
  • Statistics: localized least squares, and a finite-sample rate for linear regression

Contribution guidelines are in CONTRIBUTING.md also the website, and the organizer and contributor lists are on the website.

Two papers describe parts of current content in the library: "Lean Formalization of Generalization Error Bound by Rademacher Complexity and Dudley's Entropy Integral" (ITP 2026) and "AI4SLT: Empirical Processes in Lean 4 for Formal Statistical Learning Theory" (ICML 2026).
Can you clarify how ths is different from #Statlib ?

@Jack McCarthy Thanks for asking. I’ll distinguish the Lean code currently available for import from the projects described in the respective roadmaps.

The Statlib/ source directory contains two modules: Inference.lean and QMD.lean. Statlib’s website also lists decision theory, LAN, semiparametric and nonparametric theory, empirical processes, concentration, graphical models, high-dimensional statistics, conformal inference, and other project directions. Those roadmap and project entries are not declarations in the current Statlib/ source directory.

Our current StatsMLlib/ source directory contains 89 modules under MeasureTheory, Topology, Analysis, LinearAlgebra, Probability, LearningTheory, and Statistics, with no sorry, axiom, admit, or native_decide, which we started the works from last year (please refer to two papers on the website). The code includes covering and packing numbers; metric entropy and chaining; Efron–Stein, Hoeffding, McDiarmid, Gaussian Poincaré and log-Sobolev inequalities; sub-Gaussian processes, Dudley and truncated Dudley bounds, and Gaussian Lipschitz concentration; Hanson–Wright and matrix Bernstein; singular values, Courant–Fischer, Eckart–Young–Mirsky, Weyl, and Davis–Kahan; Rademacher complexity, symmetrization, and uniform-deviation bounds; and localized least-squares and minimax guarantees.

If Statlib reaches high-dimensional statistics, which I understand is on the roadmap, there is no reason to redo the concentration and chaining infrastructure - it is there, and we will keep it building.
